title.rendered: Unusual Things to Do When Exploring Paris Off the Beaten Path

content.rendered:
Most visitors see the Eiffel Tower or the Louvre. But if you want a memorable trip, visit Paris off the beaten path instead.

These hidden spots show you a different side of the city. And if you want to work here you may also want to learn about a work visa in France which covers job offers salary requirements paperwork and employer sponsorship.

1. Wander Along La Petite Ceinture

This old circular railway track now offers a surprising green escape through the city. Covered in wildflowers and trees, it’s a calm and secret nature trail away from the crowds.

2. Visit the Paris Sewer Museum

It may sound odd, but touring the working sewer network is a fascinating peek into the city’s infrastructure and history. It is truly one of the most unusual things to do in Paris France.

3. Stop by Maison Deyrolle

Housed in a quaint shop, this place feels like a curious cabinet of natural history, filled with old insects, birds, and other exotic specimens. A real hidden treasure among interesting things to see in Paris.

4. Walk the Promenade Plantée

Also called Coulée verte René-Dumont, this elevated park built on a former railway line is quiet, tree-lined, and full of charm. Below you’ll find local workshops and artisan studios.

5. Explore the Catacombs

Descend underground to see walls lined with bones of millions, repurposed from old cemeteries. It’s eerie, thought-provoking, and a truly unusual thing to do in Paris France.

6. Picnic at Arènes de Lutèce

Hidden in the Latin Quarter lies a small Roman amphitheater where locals play petanque and picnic. It’s quiet, free, and a lovely break—one of the off the beaten path things to do in Paris.

7. Explore Belleville’s Street Art

Head to Belleville for walls covered in vibrant street art. It’s an up-and-coming neighborhood full of culture, food, artists, and creative energy.

8. Hunt for Mini Statues of Liberty

Paris hides small replicas of the Statue of Liberty scattered around the city. Turn it into a fun city-wide scavenger hunt—lighthearted and offbeat.

9. Enjoy a Show at Musée des Arts Forains

In Bercy, this funfair museum offers vintage rides and carnival exhibits that feel like stepping into another time. A magical and little-known spot.

10. Sip Coffee with a View

The 360 Café on the 56th floor of Montparnasse Tower gives one of the best views in Paris. You’ll see all main landmarks minus the usual tourist lines.

11. See Danse de la Fontaine Emergente

At Place Augusta-Holmes, this is part sculpture, part fountain, part light installation. It comes alive at night, and is an unexpected artistic treat.

12. Visit the Miraculous Medal Chapel

A quieter chapel in the 7th arrondissement, it is known for pilgrimage visits and a peaceful atmosphere, very far from busy tourist paths.

13. Wander Covered Passages

These hidden 19th-century arcades, like Passage des Panoramas or Galerie Vivienne, are full of old-fashioned shops and stylish cafes. Many missed by casual visitors.

14. Stroll Rue Crémieux

A short pedestrian street with colorful facades. Its pastel walls make for a lovely photo spot, but early visits are best to avoid crowds.

15. Discover the Pet Cemetery

Just outside Paris in Asnières, a charming cemetery for pets including dogs, cats, and small animals. A unique and touching place not many tourists see.

Why These Spots Stand Out

  • They go beyond the usual top ten places to see in Paris France
  • Most are free or low cost
  • Many are ideal in summer when the city center is packed (things to do in Paris France in July)
  • They let you see Paris through its underground, artistic, and everyday sides
